descriptionChirho: A tribal chief or clan leader, especially of Edomite clans. Denominative from אֶלֶף II ('clan, thousand'). Used almost exclusively in the genealogical lists of Esau's descendants in Genesis 36 (vv. 15-43) and the parallel in 1 Chronicles 1:51-54, where it designates the heads of Edomite sub-clans: 'chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho' etc. Also appears in Zechariah 9:7 and 12:5-6 for chiefs/clans of Judah. The construct plural אַלּוּפֵי ('chiefs of'), the suffixed forms אַלּוּפֵיהֶם ('their chiefs'), and the comparative כְּאַלּוּף ('like a chief,' Zech 9:7) are all inflectional variants of the same noun. Multilingual glosses consistently render as chief/leader (arb: أَمِير, deu: Hauptling, fra: chef, hin: सरदार).
